initial_evidence.text: Title: Rare Variants Create Synthetic Genome-Wide Associations. Abstract sentence: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have now identified at least 2,000 common variants that appear associated with common diseases or related traits (http://www.genome.gov/gwastudies), hundreds of which have been convincingly replicated.

Title: A fine-scale map of recombination rates and hotspots across the human genome.. Abstract sentence: We present a high-resolution genetic map of the human genome, based on statistical analyses of genetic variation data, and identify more than 25,000 recombination hotspots, together with motifs and sequence contexts that play a role in hotspot activity.

Title: Rare Variants Create Synthetic Genome-Wide Associations. Abstract sentence: We propose as an alternative explanation that variants much less common than the associated one may create "synthetic associations" by occurring, stochastically, more often in association with one of the alleles at the common site versus the other allele.

Title: Rare Variants Create Synthetic Genome-Wide Associations. Abstract sentence: It is generally thought that the associated markers reflect the effect of a nearby common (minor allele frequency >0.05) causal site, which is associated with the marker, leading to extensive resequencing efforts to find causal sites.

Title: Rare Variants Create Synthetic Genome-Wide Associations. Abstract sentence: In conclusion, uncommon or rare genetic variants can easily create synthetic associations that are credited to common variants, and this possibility requires careful consideration in the interpretation and follow up of GWAS signals.
Title: Rare and common variants: twenty arguments. Abstract sentence: Genome-wide association studies have greatly improved our understanding of the genetic basis of disease risk.

Title: Rare Variants Create Synthetic Genome-Wide Associations. Abstract sentence: Here, we use simple computer simulations to show the conditions under which such synthetic associations will arise and how they may be recognized.

Title: Common and rare variants in multifactorial susceptibility to common diseases. Abstract sentence: The identification of rare variants involves the careful selection of candidate genes to examine, the availability of highly efficient resequencing techniques and the appropriate assessment of the functional consequences of the implicated variant.
